Data Storage & External Services

The application has no relational database or ORM. Job postings and postal-code coordinates are held in the Azure Cognitive Search indexes named nycjobs and zipcodes; the repository also contains JSON seed data and index schemas. The browser uses Bing Maps for map rendering. A Bing geocoding package is declared, although no active use was identified in the reviewed application code.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The MVC application queries Azure Cognitive Search directly through a search helper rather than an application database.
  • Search index creation and sample-data import are handled by a separate console utility.
  • The browser combines server-rendered MVC pages with JavaScript-driven search and map updates.

DTOs & Contracts

NYCJob is a mutable response wrapper for search results, facets, and count. NYCJobLookup is a mutable response wrapper for one Azure Search SearchDocument. Search inputs are MVC action parameters rather than dedicated request DTOs. The application uses MVC JsonResult serialization; the loader also contains a Newtonsoft.Json helper. No OpenAPI, protobuf, or GraphQL contract files were found.

Communication Patterns

The browser calls MVC actions over HTTP. The controller delegates to JobsSearch, which uses synchronous Azure Search SDK calls for queries, suggestions, and document lookup. When distance filtering is enabled, it first queries the ZIP index to obtain a location and then runs the job search. The separate console utility makes synchronous REST requests to create/delete indexes and upload documents.

No asynchronous messaging, service discovery, API gateway, client-side load balancing, retry policy, or circuit breaker was found. Search exceptions are caught in JobsSearch and generally result in a null response; there is no defined downstream fallback. No authentication or authorization checks were identified in the MVC actions. TLS settings are not established by application code; the Azure Search endpoint uses HTTPS, while deployment-side browser/API transport configuration is not specified.

Core Business Workflows

NYCJobsWeb helps users find New York City job postings by text, facets, salary, and location. Users can browse suggestions, view search results on a map, and retrieve an individual posting.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
Job postingJob SearchA public employment opportunity with searchable text, salary, posting, and location detailsUses a geographic point; may be filtered by ZIP-derived coordinates
ZIP codeLocation SearchPostal-code location record used to resolve a search centerSupplies coordinates for distance filtering of job postings
Search resultJob SearchA job posting returned with facets and a total result countReturned as a collection for a user query

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
NYCJobsWebJob Search and Location SearchNo persistent entities; queries job and ZIP search documentsAzure Cognitive Search, Bing Maps in browser
AzureSearchBackupRestoreSearch index maintenanceIndex definitions and imported document collectionsAzure Cognitive Search

The Azure Search service is the source of truth at runtime. The repository's local JSON files are sample/import content, not a separate service-owned database.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Search and filter job postings

  1. A user enters search text and optional business-title, posting-type, salary, sort, page, and location criteria.
  2. The browser posts the criteria to Home/Search.
  3. Blank search text is converted to *, so it searches the complete index.
  4. If distance filtering is enabled, the search logic looks up the ZIP code and uses the returned coordinates to form a geographic filter.
  5. Job search applies selected facets and sort options, requests ten results, facets, and a total count, then returns a NYCJob response.
  6. The browser displays results, pagination, facets, and map pins.

Workflow 2: Find a posting from suggestions

  1. The browser requests suggestions for a typed term from Home/Suggest.
  2. Azure Search performs suggestion matching against the configured suggester, with fuzzy matching enabled by default.
  3. Up to eight suggestion strings are returned and deduplicated by the controller.

Workflow 3: View job details

  1. The browser sends a selected job key to Home/LookUp.
  2. JobsSearch retrieves the document by its key from the nycjobs index.
  3. The MVC action wraps the document in NYCJobLookup and returns JSON for the detail view.

Workflow 4: Rebuild search data

  1. An operator runs the console loader with target Azure Search service settings.
  2. The utility deletes and recreates the zipcodes and nycjobs indexes from their schema files.
  3. It reads matching JSON files from the repository and uploads each file to the associated index.

Cross-Service Data Flows

The web application composes location-aware search within its own request flow: it queries the ZIP index for a geographic point and then includes that point in a query to the job index. There is no gateway or call to another application service. The console loader writes directly to both indexes. If an index request fails, JobsSearch catches the exception and returns null; there is no business fallback or degraded result contract.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User as "Job seeker" participant UI as "Browser UI" participant MVC as "HomeController" participant Logic as "JobsSearch" participant ZIP as "ZIP index" participant Jobs as "Job index" User->>UI: Enter text and filters UI->>MVC: Submit search criteria MVC->>Logic: Search(criteria) opt Distance filter requested Logic->>ZIP: Find ZIP coordinates ZIP-->>Logic: Geographic point end Logic->>Jobs: Search text and apply filters Jobs-->>Logic: Job results, facets, count Logic-->>MVC: Search response MVC-->>UI: NYCJob JSON UI-->>User: Display postings and map User->>UI: Open a posting UI->>MVC: Request posting by key MVC->>Logic: LookUp(id) Logic->>Jobs: Retrieve job document Jobs-->>Logic: Job document Logic-->>MVC: Lookup response MVC-->>UI: NYCJobLookup JSON

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • A blank search term becomes the wildcard *.
  • Search returns at most ten documents per request and includes total count and facets.
  • Business-title, posting-type, salary, and geographic-distance filters are optional.
  • Salary ranges are calculated in 50,000-unit intervals.
  • Sort modes include featured relevance, salary ascending/descending, and most recent posting.
  • Distance search runs only when the requested maximum distance is greater than zero.
  • Suggestions default to fuzzy matching and request at most eight candidates.
  • The importer deletes existing indexes before recreating and populating them; it is an operational maintenance workflow, not an end-user write workflow.
  • No dedicated validation framework, explicit authorization rules, audit trail, transaction management, or state-transition model was identified.

Version & Compatibility Risks

Both projects use legacy, non-SDK project files: the web app targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and the utility targets .NET Framework 4.5. The MVC/Razor stack and browser packages are old, and the separate utility pins Newtonsoft.Json 9.0.1 while the web app uses 10.0.3. Moving to modern .NET requires replacing or substantially adapting System.Web MVC and reviewing package compatibility.

Notable Observations

  • The web application declares 24 package entries; the separate loader declares one package entry.
  • No package lockfile or central package-management file was found; package versions are in packages.config.
  • The repository's source includes older client-side library copies in addition to NuGet package declarations.
  • No ORM, database driver, messaging, or caching dependencies were detected.

The application has no relational database, ORM, or repository layer. Its persistent data is stored in Azure Cognitive Search indexes, with job and ZIP code documents also supplied as static schema and JSON files.

Entity Model

The principal persisted models are index documents rather than application-defined ORM entities. SearchDocument is the Azure SDK's flexible document type; NYCJob and NYCJobLookup are response wrappers.

erDiagram JobDocument { string Id PK string JobId string BusinessTitle string Agency int SalaryRangeFrom int SalaryRangeTo string WorkLocation datetime PostingDate string GeoLocation } ZipCodeDocument { string ZipCode PK string City string State string County string GeoLocation }

The two Azure Search indexes do not have an enforced entity relationship. A ZIP code lookup supplies coordinates for distance filtering against job documents. The index definitions are in NYCJobsWeb/Schema_and_Data/nycjobs.schema and NYCJobsWeb/Schema_and_Data/zipcodes.schema.

Caching Strategy

No cache provider, cache annotations, TTL, or query-result cache was found. Search requests are sent directly to Azure Cognitive Search.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The web application and loader use a single Azure Search service endpoint with logically separate nycjobs and zipcodes indexes. There is no application-level database-per-service boundary, cross-service API, or CQRS implementation. Distance search reads a ZIP document to obtain a geographic point and uses it in a subsequent query against job postings. The loader is the only component that changes index definitions and bulk document contents.
